items.title: CVE-2026-114625: Arista Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL Injection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CISA adds Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-114625) to its KEV catalog.

items.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8
items.one_liner: Critical security patches for GitLab CE and EE fix multiple high-severity vulnerabilities, including CI/CD and LLM prompt flaws.
items.summary: GitLab has released versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 for Community and Enterprise Editions to address multiple security vulnerabilities and bugs. Notable fixes include a critical integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler, high-severity cross-site scripting, and improper authorization issues. Self-managed installations are strongly urged to upgrade immediately, while GitLab.com and Dedicated tenants have already been patched. The security advisory details various flaws spanning authorization bypasses, regular expression issues, and LLM prompt neutralization failures.

items.title: ConnectWise customers hit by supply-chain attack linked to compromised API secret
items.one_liner: ConnectWise suffers supply-chain breach after threat actors abuse a compromised Microsoft 365 API secret.
items.summary: ConnectWise customers are experiencing prolonged outages and hundreds of compromises after threat actors exploited a compromised API secret associated with its Cloud Backup service (formerly SkyKick). The highly sensitive multi-tenant credential allowed attackers to connect to Microsoft 365 environments, bypass multi-factor authentication, and execute automated reconnaissance and backdooring across nearly 1,000 Entra tenants. Microsoft and incident responders observed unauthorized sign-ins and malicious API activity, prompting ConnectWise to temporarily suspend multiple services while investigations continue.
key_facts: Compromised service: ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick)
items.bottom_line: A compromised multi-tenant API secret has enabled widespread unauthorized access across numerous Microsoft 365 customer tenants.

items.title: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 - Day Two Results
items.one_liner: Pwn2Own Ireland Day Two featured successful exploits against Home Assistant Green, AI infrastructure, and the Samsung Galaxy S26.
items.summary: On day two of Pwn2Own Ireland 2026, researchers targeted various connected devices, printers, and AI infrastructure platforms across multiple rounds. Notable wins included Yves Bieri taking down Home Assistant Green for $30,000, HaeJung Yang successfully hacking Dynamo in the AI infrastructure category for $40,000, and Taisic Yun breaching the Oracle Autonomous AI Database using unique zero-days and collisions. Meanwhile, attempts against Samsung's Galaxy S26 by a team utilizing Djini.ai succeeded via a confused deputy bug, while printer targets like the Brother MFC-L8970CDW proved challenging.

items.title: Open Source Snort 3 Control Channel Socket Arbitrary Command Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated local control channel socket vulnerability in Snort 3 allows low-privileged users to achieve arbitrary command execution.
items.summary: A vulnerability in the control channel socket implementation of Open Source Snort 3 allows authenticated, low-privileged local users to execute arbitrary commands and read or write process memory as the Snort 3 process user. The vulnerability stems from a lack of authentication on local connections to the Snort control channel socket. Cisco has released software updates to address the issue with no available workarounds.
items.bottom_line: Apply Cisco's software updates to fix the unauthenticated local control channel vulnerability in Snort 3.

items.title: FBI and CISA Warn of SafePay Ransomware Attacks on 600 Organizations
items.one_liner: SafePay ransomware has hit 600+ critical infrastructure organizations using VPN credential abuse and edge device flaws, per a multi-agency advisory.
items.summary: Law enforcement agencies across the US, UK, and Germany have issued a joint advisory detailing the operations of the SafePay ransomware group, which has breached over 600 organizations globally since August 2024. Operating independently without affiliates, SafePay gains initial access via exposed credentials, brute-force attacks, and VPN exploitation—frequently routing traffic through Mullvad VPN IP addresses. The group exploits known vulnerabilities in edge devices (such as Cisco, Veeam, and SonicWall) and relies on living-off-the-land tools like PsExec, PowerShell, and Mimikatz for lateral movement and data exfiltration before deploying ChaCha20 encryption for double extortion.
key_facts: Encryption Algorithm: ChaCha20 combined with RSA
items.bottom_line: The SafePay ransomware operation represents a major global threat to critical infrastructure, leveraging stolen VPN credentials and native admin tools.

claims.text: SafePay ransomware has hit 600+ organizations since 2024, using stolen credentials, VPN access and double extortion to pressure victims into paying.

items.title: State Bank of India Confirms Data Leak After 3,897 Customer Records Found on Dark Web
items.one_liner: State Bank of India confirmed a data leak exposing personal details of 3,897 customer records on the dark web.
items.summary: The State Bank of India (SBI) confirmed an incident involving the loss of certain data after 3,897 customer records containing personal information were found within a dark web dataset of roughly 375,000 records. The exposed data includes customer names, registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, residential addresses, and internal CIF identifiers, though sensitive financial details like account balances and passwords were not listed. The leak was flagged to the bank on October 16 by CERT-In and the Defense Cyber Agency, prompting SBI to engage an independent cybersecurity auditor. While the bank noted no material impact on core operations, the exposed details pose severe impersonation and phishing risks to customers.
key_facts: Exposed Records: 3,897 customer records identified out of ~375,000 total records
items.bottom_line: Exposure of customer PII and internal identifiers from India's largest bank creates immediate impersonation risks, requiring heightened vigilance against targeted phishing.

items.title: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates
items.one_liner: A key generation flaw in eMudhra's intermediate certificates resulted in trivially recoverable private keys, prompting major browser and OS vendors to block them.
items.summary: Cisco Talos has highlighted a vulnerability affecting eight intermediate certificates issued by certificate authority eMudhra due to a key generation flaw on April 30, 2025. During a wrap/unwrap step for subordinate CAs under the emSign Root TLS CA - G3 and Comodo AAA Certificate Services, the private keys dropped from 384 bits of pseudo-random security down to single or double-digit integers, making key recovery trivial. This misconfiguration allows an attacker to impersonate any website, service, or code signing verification. Major vendors including Chrome, Mozilla, Apple, and Microsoft have blocked the affected TLS and code-signing certificates, while eMudhra has revoked them and stopped issuing new certificates under its G3 root.
key_facts: CVE-2026-111943: Go programming runtime X.509 chain verification consideration
items.bottom_line: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificates suffer from critically weak cryptographic keys due to a generation flaw, allowing potential impersonation attacks if not blocked.

items.title: Qilin and INC Ransomware Groups Exploit Palo Alto Networks Flaw to Bypass MFA
items.one_liner: Qilin and INC ransomware groups are exploiting a Palo Alto Networks auth-bypass flaw to bypass MFA and compromise ESXi hypervisors.
items.summary: Ransomware groups Qilin (Spikey Scorpius) and INC (Tarnished Scorpius) are actively exploiting CVE-2026-0257, a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and Prisma Access. The flaw (CVSS 7.8) allows attackers to set up unauthorized VPN connections and bypass multi-factor authentication. Once inside, actors conduct internal reconnaissance, move laterally via RDP and SMB, and pivot to the virtualization layer to disable security controls on ESXi hypervisors. Attackers also perform offline credential dumping directly against domain controller virtual disks and target backup infrastructure.
key_facts: Threat actors: Qilin (Spikey Scorpius), INC (Tarnished Scorpius)
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-0257 is actively exploited by ransomware actors to establish unauthorized VPN sessions, pivot to virtualization layers, and dump domain credentials.

items.title: Quest Diagnostics Data Breach Exposed ‘Certain Patient Records’
items.one_liner: A medical data breach at Quest Diagnostics exposes the fragility of client platforms, requiring immediate vigilance regarding exposed healthcare records.
items.summary: Medical laboratory giant Quest Diagnostics reported a cyber breach this week affecting its Quanum Lab Services Manager platform, which clients use for test orders and results. The unauthorized access was discovered on Wednesday, prompting notifications to federal law enforcement and ongoing investigations with external cybersecurity experts. The company confirmed that certain patient records were likely accessed, though the exact scope and number of impacted patients remain undetermined. Quest emphasized that the incident is unrelated to the recent widespread PHP vulnerabilities.
key_facts: Affected Platform: Quanum Lab Services Manager

items.title: Profiling TorchNeuron (Part 1): System-level profiling on AWS Trainium.
items.one_liner: A practical guide to system-level inference profiling on AWS Trainium using TorchNeuron and PyTorch.
items.summary: This technical guide details system-level inference performance profiling on AWS Trainium chips using TorchNeuron, an open-source PyTorch backend. It demonstrates how to configure torch.profiler with the Neuron backend to capture system traces and evaluate operation execution times using key_averages() and Neuron Explorer. items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: HIGH)
items.one_liner: Palo Alto Networks has issued security guidance and mitigation steps for PAN-OS products exposed to critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. CVE-2026-109618 involves uninitialized request memory caused by improper control flow handling during out-of-memory errors via longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. While specific PAN-OS versions are affected, patches are in development, and cloud services like Cortex XCORE and WildFire Cloud have already received remediation patches. Customers with Threat Prevention subscriptions are advised to enable specific Threat IDs to protect against exploitation until official firmware updates are released.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618: PHP OOM remote code execution
CVE-2026-109619: PHP longjmp global memory corruption RCE
items.bottom_line: Palo Alto Networks products running vulnerable PHP components face RCE risks from CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, requiring threat prevention signatures or upcoming firmware patches.

items.title: Multiple Cisco Products Snort 3 Visual Basic for Applications Buffer Overflow Denial of Service Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A stack overflow in Cisco's Snort 3 VBA decompression engine lets remote attackers cause a denial of service.
items.summary: Multiple Cisco products contain a vulnerability in the Snort 3 Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) Decompression Engine due to improper range checking. An unauthenticated, remote attacker can exploit this flaw by sending crafted VBA data to trigger a stack overflow in the detection engine. This unexpected overflow forces the Snort 3 Detection Engine to restart, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. Cisco has released software updates and provided workarounds to address the vulnerability.
key_facts: Affected Component: Snort 3 VBA Decompression Engine
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated remote attackers can crash the Cisco Snort 3 detection engine via crafted VBA data, requiring immediate software updates.

items.title: How NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture Secures and Governs AI Agent Workloads at Scale
items.one_liner: NVIDIA OpenShell provides an open-source runtime architecture using hardware-enforced isolation, gateways, and policy provers to secure autonomous AI agent workloads.
items.summary: Autonomous AI agents operating over extended horizons face compounding security risks as they dynamically download code, build tools, and access infrastructure without intrinsic safety priorities. To address this, NVIDIA OpenShell provides an open-source runtime architecture that treats agent workloads as untrusted and enforces strict security controls at the infrastructure level. OpenShell consists of four primary components: a Gateway control plane for sandboxes, a Supervisor to mediate network and credential access, an isolated Sandbox environment, and a Policy Prover for formal verification. Running on NVIDIA Vera CPUs, the architecture ensures high-performance computing while guaranteeing that agent actions remain strictly bounded by organizational policies.

items.bottom_line: Securing autonomous AI agents requires moving governance out of the agent and into an infrastructure runtime that isolates execution and verifies action policies.

items.title: Ruby Fixes Three Regex Engine Bugs Responsible for Four Critical GitLab RCE Flaws
items.one_liner: Ruby patched three Onigmo regex engine memory corruption bugs that enabled four critical RCE flaws in GitLab.
items.summary: Ruby released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13 to fix three Onigmo regular expression engine bugs that caused four critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in GitLab. The bugs allow specially crafted patterns compiled from untrusted input via Regexp.new, interpolation, or similar methods to corrupt memory. GitLab patched four CVEs—including two maximum-severity 10.0 scores (CVE-2026-97229 and CVE-2026-110264)—by updating its embedded Ruby runtimes. Administrators of self-managed GitLab instances must upgrade to the latest security releases, as standard defenses like setting regex timeouts or capping pattern lengths are ineffective.

items.bottom_line: Applications compiling regexes from untrusted input are vulnerable to memory corruption via Onigmo engine bugs and must update Ruby immediately.

items.summary: PHP released emergency patches for two critical engine-level vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, carrying a CVSS score of 9.2 and allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Cloudflare observed millions of exploit attempts shortly after public disclosure, while Censys reported over 34.4 million vulnerable PHP services active online. Although security honeypots and researchers have caught massive scanning and botnet delivery traffic—such as attempts by a Mirai variant known as Potassium—no successful real-world exploitation has been officially confirmed. However, researchers have successfully developed exploits bypassing ASLR by chaining both vulnerabilities, heightening the urgency for immediate patching.

items.title: Microsoft Links ConnectWise Breach to China-Linked Group Using AI Pentesting Tool ARTEX
items.one_liner: Threat actor Storm-0940 leveraged an AI pentesting tool called ARTEX to rapidly exploit stolen ConnectWise credentials and compromise Microsoft 365 tenants.
items.summary: China-linked state-sponsored group Storm-0940 targeted 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants by exploiting stolen ConnectWise credentials at machine speed. The attackers utilized ARTEX, an open-source AI-driven penetration testing framework, to accelerate compromise, achieving privileged access to cloud infrastructure in under three hours in several instances. Before using the stolen ConnectWise credentials, the group executed password spraying attacks from IP address 144.172.64.99, generating over 151,000 failed login attempts. Following successful authentication via existing application permissions, the AI agents conducted directory reconnaissance, modified application credentials for persistence, and attempted role modifications. Microsoft advises defenders to review all service principal credential additions dating back to at least October 1 to remove potential backdoors.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are using AI frameworks like ARTEX to automate credential abuse and establish persistent backdoors in cloud environments within hours of a supply chain breach.

items.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
items.one_liner: Two CVSS 9.0 KSMBD RCE flaws were publicly dumped via AI scanning reports without upstream patches, leaving Linux servers exposed.
items.summary: Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, face two remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative that were disclosed publicly without prior mainline kernel fixes. The first flaw, ZDI-CAN-33549, is an integer underflow requiring SMB Direct, an RDMA-capable interface, and a writable share. The second flaw, ZDI-CAN-33774, enables unauthenticated pre-authentication attacks over port 445 due to a handler table assignment race condition. ZDI routed these reports using automated AI scans directly to public mailing lists without attached patches, drawing sharp criticism from stable-kernel maintainer Greg Kroah-Hartman. Because the kernel assigns CVEs only after stable-tree fixes are ready, administrators currently lack official patches and must rely on checking if the KSMBD module is active.
key_facts: Affected Component: KSMBD Linux kernel SMB server
items.bottom_line: AI-discovered kernel bugs sent directly to public mailing lists without patches create immediate zero-day risk for administrators before fixes exist.

items.title: How APT41 revived the BlackLotus bootkit to attack diplomatic organizations in Central Asia
items.one_liner: APT41-linked threat actors revived the BlackLotus bootkit under the name BlackX to target diplomatic agencies in Central Asia via the Baton Drop vulnerability.
items.summary: Security researchers uncovered an APT campaign in early 2026 targeting diplomatic organizations in Central Asian countries—specifically Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan—using a revived UEFI bootkit dubbed BlackX. The malware bears striking similarities to the BlackLotus bootkit advertised on hacking forums in 2022 and confirmed by researchers in 2023. The attackers gained administrator privileges on victim machines before deploying an RC4-encrypted installer package that exploits the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) to install custom Machine Owner Keys (MOK) and bypass Secure Boot. Once executed, the UEFI payload injects a malicious, custom-signed driver into the Windows kernel to establish persistence.
items.bottom_line: Sophisticated threat actors are reviving and adapting advanced UEFI bootkits like BlackLotus to bypass Secure Boot and compromise diplomatic networks in Central Asia.

items.one_liner: A massive data breach at P3 Global Intel unmasks 1.5 million anonymous crime tips, forcing Toronto Crime Stoppers to halt submissions entirely.
items.summary: Toronto Crime Stoppers has suspended phone, web, and app tip submissions after a data breach at P3 Global Intel exposed over 1.5 million anonymous crime reports spanning 25 years. The incident underscores the systemic risks of relying on third-party tip management platforms.

items.title: CVE-2026-115895 - Happy DOM: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33943: unsanitized import alias leads to host code execution
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-115895 in Happy DOM allows host code execution via unsanitized ESM import aliases when JavaScript evaluation is enabled.
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-115895, has been identified in Happy DOM versions 17.0.0 through 21.0.4. The flaw stems from an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33943 within `packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.ts`, where named ECMAScript module import aliases are accepted without validating if they are valid JavaScript binding identifiers before insertion into generated destructuring bindings. When JavaScript evaluation is enabled, an attacker can supply malicious HTML or module sources with invalid aliases that compile into valid default initializers, resulting in arbitrary code execution in the Node.js host process. The vulnerability can be triggered via JSON module import attributes and is patched in version 21.0.4.
items.bottom_line: Happy DOM versions prior to 21.0.4 allow remote code execution in the Node.js host through unvalidated ESM import aliases under malicious input.

items.summary: F5 and open-source NGINX developers have published advisories detailing multiple medium-severity vulnerabilities affecting NGINX Open Source prior to versions 1.31.7 and 1.30.6, including remote code execution risks. CVE-2026-97205 involves a use-after-free vulnerability in asynchronous file I/O (AIO) processing of Server Side Includes (SSI) pages, allowing potential code execution under specific ASLR bypass conditions. Additional issues include a session forgery flaw in TLS session tickets (CVE-2026-97629), a request body injection vulnerability in HTTP/3 proxy buffering (CVE-2026-95101), a heap buffer overflow during regex map evaluations (CVE-2026-93479), and a buffer overflow when combining alias with rewrite directives (CVE-2026-15176).
key_facts: CVE-2026-97205: Use-after-free in AIO, medium severity
CVE-2026-97629: Session forgery via TLS tickets, medium severity
CVE-2026-95101: Request body injection in HTTP/3, medium severity
CVE-2026-93479: Heap buffer overflow in script evaluation, medium severity
CVE-2026-15176: Buffer overflow with alias and rewrite, medium severity
items.bottom_line: Several vulnerabilities in NGINX Open Source prior to 1.31.7 and 1.30.6, including use-after-free and buffer overflows, expose servers to potential remote code execution.

items.title: CVE-2026-58202 - OpenReception: Confirmation-email links built from the request Host enable pending-account takeover via `POST /api/auth/resend-confirmation`
items.one_liner: OpenReception prior to v2.0.0 is vulnerable to pending-account takeover via Host header injection during password confirmation resends.
items.summary: A vulnerability, CVE-2026-58202, exists in OpenReception appointment booking software prior to version 2.0.0, where account confirmation links in emails are constructed from the unvalidated request Host header rather than a trusted tenant domain. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via the POST /api/auth/resend-confirmation endpoint by injecting a malicious Host header alongside a pending invitee's email address. When the invitee clicks the password/account confirmation link generated in the resulting email, the one-time token is sent directly to the attacker. The attacker can then complete the account registration on the legitimate tenant domain and register an attacker-controlled passkey to fully hijack the account before the victim can use it. The issue can be mitigated via front proxy restrictions or updated to version 2.0.0.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can exploit Host header injection in OpenReception's resend-confirmation endpoint to intercept account activation tokens and execute full takeovers of pending accounts.

items.title: CVE-2026-79982 - Out-of-bounds write in the USB Bluetooth HCI transport class when a controller-to-host HCI packet exceeds the bulk endpoint maximum packet size
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-79982 exposes Bluetooth stacks to remote memory corruption or denial of service via unvalidated USB HCI transfer buffers exceeding maximum packet sizes.
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-79982, has been discovered in the Bluetooth HCI USB transport class of Zephyr's new USB device stack (subsys/usb/device_next/class/bt_hci.c). The flaw involves an out-of-bounds write occurring when a controller-to-host HCI packet exceeds the bulk endpoint maximum packet size of 64 bytes. Because the transfer buffer is allocated from a fixed pool (bt_hci_ep_pool) without boundary validation in net_buf_add_mem(), oversized packets—such as mandatory 70-byte initialization commands or malicious over-the-air fragments—overflow into adjacent memory slots. On production builds with assertions disabled (CONFIG_ASSERT=n), this silently corrupts memory and can lead to arbitrary code execution by an unauthenticated attacker within Bluetooth range; with assertions enabled, it causes a denial of service via system panic. The fix introduces a properly sized separate pool, bt_hci_tx_pool, to handle controller-to-host packets.
key_facts: CVE-2026-79982: Out-of-bounds write in USB Bluetooth HCI transport class
items.bottom_line: An unauthenticated remote attacker within Bluetooth range can trigger an out-of-bounds write via oversized HCI packets in Zephyr's USB Bluetooth transport stack, leading to RCE or DoS.

items.title: CVE-2026-79977 - WireGuard peer endpoint learned from unauthenticated transport-data messages allows off-path tunnel hijack in Zephyr
items.one_liner: Zephyr's WireGuard implementation is susceptible to tunnel hijacking via unauthenticated UDP packets, leading to a complete loss of availability.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in the Zephyr RTOS implementation of WireGuard allows unauthenticated off-path attackers to hijack VPN tunnels. By sending a single spoofed UDP datagram with an arbitrary receiver index, an attacker can redirect the peer endpoint to a malicious address. This results in a persistent loss of availability for the tunnel, as the legitimate peer is bypassed and fails to re-authenticate. The vulnerability exists because the endpoint is updated based on unauthenticated transport-data messages.
items.bottom_line: If you are using WireGuard on Zephyr, your tunnel can be hijacked by any off-path attacker who can send a single UDP packet to your listener port.

items.one_liner: Python developers using older versions of Hugging Face Datasets face an RCE risk when loading untrusted data via the deprecated pandas builder.
items.summary: Hugging Face Datasets through version 5.1.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-57845, via the deprecated pandas packaged builder. items.title: CVE-2026-54668 - Kitodo.Production: XXE in XMLUtils EAD/XML upload parsers (parseXMLString / getNumberOfEADElements / checkIfXmlIsWellFormed lack secure JAXP config)
items.one_liner: Upgrade Kitodo.Production to version 3.9.2 to patch CVE-2026-54668, an authenticated XXE vulnerability in XML upload parsers.
items.summary: A critical XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-54668, affects Kitodo.Production prior to version 3.9.2. The flaw exists in the org.kitodo.production.helper.XMLUtils utility methods (parseXMLString, getNumberOfEADElements, and checkIfXmlIsWellFormed), which instantiate JAXP parsers without secure configurations or disabled DOCTYPE declarations. An authenticated attacker who uploads a crafted EAD/XML file via the process creation dialog can trigger local file disclosure and outbound Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The issue has been patched in version 3.9.2.
items.bottom_line: Unsecured JAXP XML parsers in Kitodo.Production allow authenticated users to execute XXE and SSRF attacks.

items.title: CVE-2026-53942 - Conda Organization Infrastructure: Pwn Request in update workflow allows PR-controlled template rendering with SYNC_TOKEN
items.one_liner: Audit GitHub Actions workflows that checkout PR-controlled code and process templates with elevated tokens.
items.summary: A GitHub Actions workflow vulnerability exists in the conda/conda repository prior to commit 9c0f238, allowing attackers to achieve a Pwn Request chain. The workflow handles issue comments containing specific render commands by checking out a PR-controlled repository and branch using a privileged `SYNC_TOKEN`. items.bottom_line: Unsanitized Jinja2 template rendering in conda update workflows allowed privileged token compromise via malicious PRs.

items.one_liner: Update Goobi viewer to patch Content-Disposition path traversal risks leading to Tomcat RCE.
items.summary: Goobi viewer versions 24.03 to before 26.05 contain a path traversal vulnerability in ExternalFilesDownloader.getFilename() due to improperly validated Content-Disposition headers. When targeting the web application directory under a Tomcat server, this results in remote code execution.
items.bottom_line: Unvalidated Content-Disposition headers in Goobi viewer allow remote code execution via path traversal.

items.title: CVE-2026-53921 - odhcpd: Stack buffer overflow in DHCPv6 IA reply serialization (2 independent sites)
items.one_liner: OpenWrt routers running odhcpd prior to 25.12 are vulnerable to unauthenticated RCE via a malformed DHCPv6 request.
items.summary: OpenWrt's odhcpd prior to version 25.12 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in its DHCPv6 IA reply serialization handler. Two independent overflow sites in the code chain write past a fixed 512-byte stack buffer (pdbuf) when a DHCPv6 request includes sufficient IA options to exhaust reply space. Because odhcpd runs as root and embedded targets often lack stack canaries and ASLR, unauthenticated remote attackers can achieve code execution via a single UDP packet. The vulnerability has been resolved in version 25.12.
items.bottom_line: Update OpenWrt to version 25.12 immediately to fix critical stack buffer overflows in odhcpd's DHCPv6 handler that allow remote code execution as root.

items.title: [0day-rubbish] Royal Render 9.1.26b: default-unauthenticated job submission on rrServer TCP 7773 reaches worker-side shell execution as the worker identity, measured root (8.1 High)
items.one_liner: Royal Render 9.1.26b ships with unauthenticated TCP job submission, letting attackers execute arbitrary shell scripts on worker nodes.
items.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in Royal Render version 9.1.26b allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution on worker nodes. The central scheduler (rrServer) runs on TCP port 7773 and lacks authentication by default, as shipped configuration files set nTCPRequiresAuth to false and leave the whitelist empty. Malicious job submissions can specify an Execute job type with a shell script path (`.sh`), which the worker evaluates via a shell template. The vulnerability enables arbitrary command execution under the worker's system privileges.
key_facts: CWE: CWE-306, CWE-1188, CWE-73, CWE-250, CWE-284, CWE-1392
items.bottom_line: Default-unauthenticated job submissions in Royal Render rrServer lead to direct remote code execution on worker nodes.

items.one_liner: A fatal chloroform leak at Saraca Laboratories in Telangana killed two workers, prompting an immediate state-ordered shutdown of the plant.

items.title: Pulse of the Street: earnings strengthen, but stocks lose ground
items.one_liner: Surging crude oil prices and inflation fears triggered a sharp correction across Indian equities, especially small-caps, overshadowing accelerating Q2 corporate earnings growth.

items.title: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust
items.one_liner: PerMIT provides a formally verified memory architecture to protect your multi-agent LLM systems from context poisoning and prompt injection.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced PerMIT, a memory architecture designed to secure persistent memory for LLM agents against injection and poisoning attacks. PerMIT uses machine-checked integrity theorems in Lean 4 and a finite memory interface where only user inputs and gate-confirmed values are trusted. Across simulations and benchmarks like Trojan Hippo and $	au^2$-bench, PerMIT prevents direct memory injection while allowing agents to safely accumulate and share knowledge. This design limits environment-derived vulnerabilities to auditable decisions made by humans or verifiers.

items.title: Model-intrinsic, Weight-level, and Training-free Spectral Fingerprinting for Large Language Models
items.one_liner: A new training-free weight-level spectral fingerprinting method enables robust ownership auditing and identification of open-weight LLMs.
items.summary: To protect open-weight LLM ownership and audit models reliably without relying on vulnerable query responses or activations, researchers introduce a model-intrinsic, weight-level, and training-free spectral fingerprinting framework. The method derives compact fingerprints by analyzing singular-value distributions of projection weights within gated feed-forward networks, aggregating them via depth-wise segmented pooling, and comparing them using linear centered kernel alignment. The approach is entirely training-free and shows stable similarity results across post-training modifications like instruction tuning, quantization, pruning, and distillation.
items.bottom_line: Spectral fingerprinting of LLM weight matrices provides a robust, training-free mechanism for ownership verification that resists quantization and distillation.

items.title: AgentPolicyForge: From Executable Environments to Policy Benchmarks and Adaptive Guards
items.one_liner: AgentPolicyForge introduces an executable environment framework to benchmark agent policies and train adaptive guards that reduce attack success.
items.summary: Researchers introduced AgentPolicyForge, a framework designed to construct policy benchmarks and iteratively train adaptive guards for customized AI agent deployments. The framework utilizes executable environments to generate tool-call data across 10 policy families, forming the PolicyGym dataset comprising 698 training scenarios and 254 held-out test scenarios. By recording tool execution outcomes and testing argument-level and context-level compliance, the framework enables iterative fine-tuning using balanced, environment-verified examples. Evaluations on PolicyGym show that the guard-based configuration achieves a 40-44% relative reduction in attack success rate compared to prompt-based instructions alone.

items.title: Social-HUMINT: An LLM-Augmented Unified Framework for Measuring Social Media Exposure
items.one_liner: Social-HUMINT provides an LLM-augmented multi-agent pipeline that accurately profiles individuals from social media data to measure social engineering exposure.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced Social-HUMINT, an LLM-augmented unified framework that bridges SOCMINT and Cyber-HUMINT to measure social media exposure and profiling risks. The framework operationalizes a taxonomy of 38 capabilities as a multi-agent pipeline that extracts personal attributes, infers undisclosed traits, and predicts engagement susceptibilities from public user data. Evaluations showed high profiling accuracy, with extraction reaching F1 = 97.3% and inferred attributes scoring 4.73 out of 5, outperforming rule-based baselines. The methodology enables security analysts and defenders to quantify human exposure and social engineering vulnerabilities prior to active exploitation.
items.bottom_line: Social-HUMINT combines SOCMINT and Cyber-HUMINT into an automated LLM framework that accurately profiles user exposure to social engineering risks.

items.title: JANUS: Agentic Cross-Language Fuzzing Harness Generation for Android Native Libraries
items.one_liner: JANUS uses an autonomous agentic workflow to automate cross-language JNI fuzzing harness generation for Android native libraries, uncovering new vulnerabilities in pre-installed vendor apps.
items.summary: Modern Android apps heavily rely on native libraries using the Java Native Interface (JNI), which connects the memory-safe Android Runtime to unsafe C/C++ code and frequently leads to severe vulnerabilities. Existing fuzzing harness generation tools fail to handle closed-source cross-language API usage because precise program analysis across the JNI boundary does not scale and they cannot construct complex composite objects. To solve this, researchers introduced JANUS, an agentic approach that synthesizes cross-language JNI-aware fuzzing harnesses by iteratively resolving call dependencies and bottom-up argument assembly. Evaluated on 44 popular apps covering 21,386 JNI methods, JANUS produced 6,094 valid harnesses—5.9 times more than state-of-the-art tools—and uncovered six previously unknown vulnerabilities in pre-installed closed-source native libraries from vendors like Xiaomi, Vivo, and Samsung.
items.bottom_line: Automated agentic JNI fuzzing can discover critical zero-days in pre-installed Android vendor libraries by overcoming the limitations of traditional cross-language harness generation.

items.title: Not Where You Think: Protecting Location Privacy Against Reasoning-Based Geolocation
items.one_liner: A new proactive defense tool called GeoShift protects image location privacy against advanced reasoning models by strategically altering distinctive visual clues.
items.summary: Researchers have developed GeoTrace, a structured reasoning attack that exposes how large reasoning models perform fine-grained image localization by extracting small, distinctive visual clues. Evaluating GeoTrace on a worldwide benchmark of 525 ordinary images revealed that Gemini-3-Flash and GPT-5-mini could localize 25.71% and 16.95% of images within 1 km, respectively. To counteract this privacy risk, the authors created GeoShift, a proactive defense mechanism that preserves broad scene properties while altering high-impact geo-revealing clues. Experiments demonstrate that GeoShift reduces street-level localization accuracy down to 2.48% for GPT-5-mini and 3.81% for Gemini-3-Flash without degrading overall visual quality.
items.bottom_line: GeoShift effectively prevents reasoning-based AI models from geolocating ordinary photos by obfuscating high-impact visual clues while preserving scene aesthetics.

items.title: PhishGen: Understanding LLM Capabilities in Automated Phishing Website Generation
items.one_liner: PhishGen evaluation reveals commercial LLMs generate functional phishing pages at scale, outperforming uncensored models.
items.summary: Researchers have developed PhishGen, a framework evaluating the appearance fidelity and functionality of LLM-generated phishing websites across commercial, open-source, and uncensored models. The study found that while 96.2% of safeguard-bypassing outputs rendered visually, only 38.7% successfully completed a full credential-harvesting pipeline. Surprisingly, commercial models like GPT-4.1 vastly outperformed uncensored models, achieving up to 94.1% functional success rates compared to under 45.4% for uncensored variants. PhishGen highlights how frontier LLMs enable scalable phishing page creation and provides insights for building hybrid detection systems.
items.bottom_line: Frontier models like GPT-4.1 achieve high functional success in automated phishing generation, posing significant risks that bypass simple text filters.

items.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: AfterDeleteBench demonstrates that LLM agents often retain and reconstruct deleted secrets from persistent memory or descendants, requiring behavioral audits rather than simple storage deletions.
items.summary: Many LLM agents maintain persistent external memory or state summaries, meaning that deleting an original record does not necessarily remove information inherited by its descendants. Researchers introduced AfterDeleteBench to audit post-deletion information persistence in fixed-weight LLM agents by comparing exposed-then-deleted agents with unexposed controls. In tests using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a single query successfully recovered deleted secrets in roughly two thirds of cases, while exact reconstruction from component parts succeeded 62-99% of the time across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3 models even when the verbatim secret string was absent. The study shows that provenance-aware closure successfully eliminates observed recovery, whereas exact-literal write filters cannot erase information already present in model state.
key_facts: Evaluated models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen, Mistral, Phi-3
items.bottom_line: Deleting records from an LLM agent's memory does not guarantee information removal, as agents can reconstruct deleted secrets from remaining state and derived descendants.

items.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
items.one_liner: AgentTriage offers an executable contract for deterministic, replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous AI agent tool-use runtimes.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced AgentTriage, an executable contract designed to provide replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous AI agent runtimes. Because tool-use agents write files, execute code, and send data through incompatible runtime interfaces without explaining resulting security events, AgentTriage uses runtime overlays to normalize observations and a deterministic pipeline to construct a typed provenance graph. This enables diagnosis and claims binding to recorded evidence to be recomputed without language-model judgment. Evaluated across five runtimes and 120 adjudicated cases, the system achieved 0.858 grounded joint diagnosis, 0.966 required-evidence coverage, and a 0.036 unsupported-claim rate, demonstrating high precision for security tracing.
items.bottom_line: AgentTriage eliminates LLM judgment calls during security incident diagnosis by normalizing tool execution traces into a deterministic provenance graph across disparate agent runtimes.

items.title: MPIDetector: Detecting Multi-modal Prompt Injection via LLM-based Reasoning
items.one_liner: MPIDetector is a new LLM-driven reasoning framework that achieves near-perfect detection of multi-modal prompt injections across text, vision, and web-agent inputs.
items.summary: With the integration of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in applications, prompt injection has become a critical security threat that bypasses traditional signature- and perplexity-based filters. To address this, researchers proposed MPIDetector, a detection framework leveraging MLLMs' intrinsic reasoning capabilities via few-shot In-Context Learning without requiring fine-tuning. Evaluated across benchmark datasets containing textual and visual malicious categories, MPIDetector achieved up to 90.91% accuracy and 100% recall on text, up to 99.28% accuracy with 100% precision on visual tasks, and a 99.80% detection rate against 500 obfuscated web-agent injections (WebInject).
items.bottom_line: LLM-driven in-context reasoning provides a highly accurate cross-modal defense against sophisticated text and vision prompt injections.

items.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
items.one_liner: LLM agents risk leaking confidential data by assembling sensitive conclusions across multiple authorized documents.
items.summary: Researchers have quantified the mosaic effect in LLM agents, where systems retrieve information from accessible documents and assemble sensitive conclusions to create confidentiality leaks. Testing three LLM agents across 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military examples revealed that even under benign queries, GPT-5.6-Sol disclosed forbidden composites in 7.08% of simulated answers. Adding visible classification headers and aggregation rules reduced disclosures, but unsafe leaks persisted in 32.37% of simulated answers, demonstrating that confidential data leaks via mosaic events remain a critical failure mode.
items.bottom_line: Mosaic-style inference allows LLM agents to inadvertently leak sensitive information across documents, bypassing standard access controls.

items.title: AutoFraming: Synthesizing Dynamic Frames of C Code with LLMs
items.one_liner: AutoFraming improves formal verification of C code by using code property graphs to guide LLMs in generating accurate memory frame specifications.
items.summary: AutoFraming is a new LLM-based tool designed to synthesize formal ACSL frame specifications for C code, addressing a gap in existing automated verification. By analyzing code property graphs (CPGs) to guide the LLM, the tool captures memory region-separation constraints and data dependencies. The method achieved a 92.9% success rate on a benchmark of real-world functions, significantly outperforming current state-of-the-art techniques.
items.bottom_line: Integrating code property graphs with LLMs allows for highly accurate automated generation of formal frame specifications, a critical component for secure C code verification.

items.title: ARCANA: A Benchmark for Abstraction and Analogical Reasoning
items.one_liner: A new benchmark and reasoning framework (ConceptSIR) exposes and targets the limitations of LLMs in far analogical reasoning.
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus of ANAlogy (ARCANA) benchmark to test far analogical reasoning between superficially dissimilar domains and abstract grid-based transformations. Human studies confirm people solve these tasks reliably, while large language models display a clear performance gap and systematic failures. To mitigate this, the authors propose ConceptSIR, a reasoning framework leveraging concept slippage, introspection, and reflection that helps standard LLMs solve previously failed tasks. All benchmark code and datasets are made publicly available.
items.bottom_line: LLMs struggle significantly with far analogical reasoning, but structured frameworks like ConceptSIR can help bridge the performance gap.

items.title: LLM-Based Exogenous World Modeling for Dynamic Scheduling
items.one_liner: Using an LLM as an exogenous world model for dynamic scheduling significantly reduces tardiness across job-shop benchmarks.
items.summary: To handle uncertain job arrivals and mitigate nonlinear tardiness in dynamic scheduling, researchers propose an Afterstate World-Model Planning (AWMP) framework that uses a pretrained large language model as an exogenous world model. The model separates deterministic shop floor transitions from uncertain job arrivals via an afterstate decomposition, querying the LLM compactly only for the latter. A surprise-triggered refresh mechanism and online residual self-calibration help manage forecast errors and nonstationary distributions. Benchmarks show that AWMP reduces weighted tardiness by 6-21% on job shops and 22-46% on flexible job shops compared to traditional priority-dispatching rules.
items.bottom_line: Integrating pretrained LLMs into structured afterstate world models improves scheduling efficiency and lowers downstream delays in complex manufacturing environments.

items.title: Self-Evolving Static Analysis via LLM Pseudo-Labeling
items.one_liner: SESAA is an LLM-driven framework that automatically evolves static analysis rules and Joern queries using critic feedback without requiring ground-truth labels.
items.summary: Researchers introduced SESAA, a framework that enables Large Language Model agents to self-evolve static analysis rules without human-authored baseline rules or ground-truth labels. Furthermore, when tested on real-world Python projects, queries induced from prior code successfully detected 10 of 19 subsequent CVEs.

items.title: Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
items.one_liner: Using terminal database checks as reinforcement learning rewards significantly improves AI agent reliability and repeatable success on complex tasks.
items.summary: Researchers have developed ThinkingBox, a framework that evaluates AI agent performance by comparing terminal database states against expected outcomes. The approach significantly boosted repeatable success rates on complex agentic tasks outside the standard benchmark by filtering out hopeless or already-solved training scenarios using offline policy-relative difficulty.
items.bottom_line: Turning executable database checks into post-training RL rewards sharply increases reliable task completion for large language model agents.

items.title: LiteLLM hit by second supply chain attack this year, users urged to rotate credentials
items.one_liner: LiteLLM's second supply chain compromise in 2026 pushes credential-stealing malware via PyPI and Docker, requiring immediate secret rotation for anyone who installed v1.107.0.
items.summary: LiteLLM suffered its second supply chain attack of the year when version v1.107.0 was pushed to PyPI and Docker registries, embedding compiled malware designed to harvest cloud credentials, developer secrets, and AI service API keys. The compromise originated from stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens used by attackers to manipulate the release pipeline and delete workflow logs. Security researchers warn that updating to a safe version is insufficient; all developers who installed the compromised package must rotate their credentials immediately. The malicious code inserts itself into Python startup files, ensuring execution whenever Python starts up in an affected environment.

items.title: USN-8951-1: c-ares vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: Multiple denial of service and memory allocation vulnerabilities in c-ares impact multiple Ubuntu LTS versions.
items.summary: Several vulnerabilities have been identified in c-ares, an asynchronous DNS client library, affecting various Ubuntu releases. These flaws include improper parsing of SOA replies and sortlist strings, inadequate limits on DNS compression pointer hops and name lengths, and a lack of proper record count validation before memory allocation when processing DNS responses. A remote attacker could exploit these issues to cause denial of service via excessive resource consumption or crashes, or potentially execute arbitrary code. Ubuntu has published security updates to resolve these vulnerabilities across supported package versions.

items.summary: A critical vulnerability has been disclosed in the RingRTC library for Signal affecting versions prior to 2.72.0, where an attacker can saturate a call's finite state machine queue. items.one_liner: State-sponsored Russian hackers leveraged an undocumented Yggdrasil mesh network backdoor called MythicRatatoskr before executing a destructive wiper attack in Ukraine.

items.title: Why the AI Attack Surface Extends Your Stack
items.one_liner: Enterprise AI integrations expand the attack surface beyond models to surrounding tools, APIs, and cloud infrastructure, enabling complex multi-layer attack chains.
items.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into enterprise workflows significantly expands the traditional application security attack surface beyond the model itself. Security leaders must map what AI systems can access and execute realistic attack scenarios across all underlying infrastructure layers.
items.bottom_line: Enterprise AI security requires mapping full stack integrations and testing realistic attack chains rather than relying solely on traditional perimeter defenses or model safety scans.

items.title: CVE-2026-58497 - Uni-CLI: Legacy HTTP MCP transport accepted browser-originated localhost requests
items.one_liner: Uni-CLI versions prior to 0.225.2 allow malicious web pages to execute local MCP tool calls via an unvalidated legacy HTTP transport.
items.summary: Uni-CLI prior to version 0.225.2 improperly accepted browser-originated requests on its legacy HTTP Model Context Protocol (MCP) transport. The endpoint failed to validate incoming browser Origin headers on loopback requests, allowing malicious web pages to send CORS simple POST requests to the local /mcp endpoint and invoke tools/call actions. The issue affected the legacy stateless HTTP path, whereas the newer Streamable HTTP transport already correctly enforced the browser-to-localhost boundary. The vulnerability has been resolved in version 0.225.2.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade Uni-CLI to version 0.225.2 to prevent cross-origin local access to the legacy HTTP MCP transport.

items.title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
items.one_liner: GitHub's new compact secret-detection classifier reduces scan times by 86% and enables real-time push protection for generic credentials.
items.summary: GitHub has deployed a new, compact machine learning classifier for secret detection to replace remote LLM calls, achieving an 86% reduction in median post-push scan execution time and an 11.5% higher owner-weighted alert precision. items.title: There's only so much code: the rise in vulnerability numbers
items.summary: Frontier AI models (like Mythos) are rapidly mining decades of technical debt across ubiquitous legacy libraries, driving monthly Microsoft Patch Tuesday vulnerability advisories up more than tenfold (reaching 1,415 this month). This volume is overwhelming open-source maintainers and putting pressure on the traditional 90-day coordinated disclosure model. items.title: IndiGo extends cancellation of Saudi flights as regional tensions escalate: Indian mission
items.one_liner: IndiGo extends flight suspensions to Saudi Arabia amid security escalation and Houthi attacks.
items.summary: The Indian Embassy in Riyadh has announced that IndiGo has extended the suspension of its flights to and from Saudi Arabia due to escalating regional security concerns and recent Houthi attacks. Flights to Riyadh are canceled through October 31, while services to Jeddah, Dammam, and Madinah remain suspended until October 27. The disruptions follow attacks targeting regional infrastructure, including an incident at Dammam's airport that killed an Indian national, prompting the Ministry of External Affairs to coordinate the return of affected pilgrims.

items.title: Legal action ordered against officials over irregularities in voter list in Pilibhit
items.one_liner: Uttar Pradesh election authorities order legal action against officials over severe voter list manipulation and data discrepancies in Pilibhit.
items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer ordered legal and departmental action against current and former election officials following major discrepancies in voter lists for the Pilibhit Assembly Constituency. Investigations revealed that a computer operator entered 13,779 Form-8 applications between May and August 2026 without corresponding physical office records, resulting in 10,470 erroneous entries where searching one voter's EPIC number displayed another person's details. The Election Commission of India directed that legal action be initiated under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, while computer support staff are slated for termination.

items.bottom_line: Electoral roll discrepancies and missing application records in Pilibhit have triggered criminal and departmental penalties against responsible election officials.

items.one_liner: A growing paper-leak scandal involving Maharashtra public service exams highlights ongoing integrity challenges in Indian government recruitment processes.
items.summary: The Special Investigation Team probing the MPSC Drug Inspector recruitment exam paper leak arrested another commission official, Rohit Kolatakke, bringing total arrests to 13. Investigators found Kolatakke obtained the confidential question set from previously arrested under-secretary Abhijit Lendve through an intermediary network involving coaching institute operators. The MPSC cancelled the recruitment process in August after 488 candidates had already been interviewed for 154 vacancies, vowing to hold a fresh examination. A special court recently rejected a bail application for an intermediary, noting evidence pointing to systemic corruption.

items.title: Government to modify labour survey to capture gig economy, unpaid household workers
items.one_liner: India's revised Periodic Labour Force Survey will begin tracking gig economy workers and unpaid domestic labor starting January 2027.
items.summary: The Union government of India has announced significant structural modifications to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) starting January 2027 to capture digital platform workers and unpaid domestic labor. Administered by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), the revised survey introduces a dedicated Second Stage Stratum (SSS) to identify households with digital platform workers and adds specific metrics for unpaid household chores, caregiving, volunteering, and trainee work. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation has invited public and expert feedback on the concept note within a 15-day window. These changes aim to address long-standing omissions in measuring women's unpaid labor and the evolving gig economy workforce.
key_facts: Executing agency: National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)
items.bottom_line: India is overhauling its Periodic Labour Force Survey framework to officially track digital platform workers and unmeasured unpaid household labor.

items.title: ReDence: A Hybrid Agentic and Decision-Model Framework for Rapid, Evidence-Grounded Detection of Modern Social Engineering Scams
items.one_liner: ReDence is an open-source hybrid AI framework for fast, evidence-grounded detection of social engineering scams.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced ReDence, an open-source hybrid framework designed for rapid, evidence-grounded detection of online social engineering scams. ReDence combines a fine-tuned multimodal agentic Investigator model for investigative planning with a specialized Decider model for binary and action-selection decisions. items.title: Bridging the Closed-World Gap: Interpretable Anomaly Detection via a Hybrid TSK-FCM Ensemble on the BETH Dataset
items.one_liner: Explore the Hybrid TSK-FCM Ensemble framework to improve interpretable kernel-level anomaly detection against novel botnets.
items.summary: To resolve the paradox where supervised models generalize poorly to out-of-distribution (OoD) attacks and unsupervised models experience high false-alarm rates, researchers introduced a Hybrid Fuzzy Ensemble for cybersecurity anomaly detection on the BETH kernel-level dataset. The framework combines a gradient-optimized Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) fuzzy classifier to handle known insider threats with a parallel Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) module to detect geometric anomalies. To overcome the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional feature spaces, the authors incorporated a robust Min Distance metric. The approach achieved a state-of-the-art AUROC of 0.9951 on the BETH test set.
items.bottom_line: A hybrid fuzzy ensemble using a robust Min Distance metric achieves 0.9951 AUROC on the BETH dataset.

items.title: Beyond End-to-End Recovery: Towards a Better Understanding of LLM Steganography via Rolewise Decomposition
items.one_liner: A rolewise decomposition framework for LLM steganography uncovers hidden encoding and decoding discrepancies missed by end-to-end metrics.
items.summary: To better evaluate steganographic message transmission in large language models, researchers propose a rolewise decomposition framework that separately examines encoder transmission representation, decoder recovery, and deterministic verification, moving beyond simple end-to-end (E2E) recovery metrics. Analyzing 7,200 encoder responses revealed 168 verifiable encodings that decoders missed, alongside 706 responses containing private messages reconstructed via unspecified word-length or token-initial patterns. These findings show that E2E metrics obscure critical distinctions between encoding and decoding failures, helping security researchers design better mitigations for LLM steganography risks.
items.bottom_line: Evaluating steganography via decoupled rolewise analysis reveals hidden message representations and failure modes that standard E2E recovery checks completely miss.

items.title: CrashGym: Measuring the Decision Value of Experimentation for LLM Agents in Counterfactual Market Crashes
items.one_liner: CrashGym offers quantitative proof that giving LLM trading agents sandbox experimentation environments radically cuts decision regret during market crashes.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced CrashGym, a deterministic, replayable limit-order-book simulator designed to measure whether experimentation by LLM agents improves critical market-intervention decisions. The simulator tests agent choices between deleveraging interventions and liquidity backstops during shock-triggered counterfactual market crashes by letting them query lab experiments. In a prospective study, laboratory access reduced the mean regret of agent deployments by 57.4% compared to observe-only baselines. The framework proves that simulation environments can effectively quantify avoided decision losses for autonomous agents.
key_facts: Regret Reduction: 57.4% decrease in mean regret with laboratory access
items.bottom_line: Providing LLM financial agents with simulated laboratory access dramatically reduces their decision-making errors during market shocks.

items.title: MCP vs CLI for AI Agents: A Comparative Analysis of Tool Integration Strategies for Autonomous Systems
items.one_liner: Comparing CLI and MCP tool integration strategies highlights trade-offs for autonomous AI agent governance and efficiency.
items.summary: A comparative analysis of CLI and MCP tool integration paradigms for autonomous AI agents reveals that CLI excels in single-user local workflows, whereas MCP fulfills advanced requirements like fine-grained access control, credential isolation, and structured audit. The paper recommends hybrid architectures for production systems.

items.title: The Price of Safety: Benign-Case Utility and Token Overhead of Memory-Poisoning Defenses in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Evaluating LLM agent security defenses reveals that read-time rerankers impose hidden utility and accuracy costs on benign traffic.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated the benign-case utility and token overhead costs of four memory-poisoning defenses in LLM agents using a consistent testing harness. While write-time defenses like sanitization and provenance checking incurred no accuracy cost and low token overhead, read-time rerankers dropped memory from 45% of questions and reduced core accuracy by 4.4 points. Stacking all four defenses raised token overhead to 4.1% without compounding accuracy costs. The findings demonstrate that defensive architectures impose hidden utility penalties on benign traffic that attack-success evaluations miss.
items.bottom_line: Memory-poisoning defenses for LLM agents carry measurable costs on normal traffic, with read-time rerankers significantly degrading core task accuracy.

items.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
items.one_liner: Diffusion language model agents can successfully communicate via hidden latent state transfers, where transfer timing matters more than exchange frequency.
items.summary: Researchers investigating multi-agent diffusion language models show that agents can communicate via continuous hidden messages passed during denoising trajectories, rather than just post-decoding text. In experiments where a sender compresses its denoising state into four signed dense vectors consumed by a receiver, removing or deranging the message causes sharp performance drops on tasks like Tiny-A2D, Dream-7B, and QASC. Furthermore, timing experiments reveal a surprising temporal dynamic: a single late transfer of latent states can outperform multiple recurrent message exchanges.
items.bottom_line: Multi-agent diffusion LMs can leverage continuous latent message passing during generation, proving that hidden state communication is both viable and highly effective.

items.title: Forging More Tasks into Better Harnesses: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing
items.one_liner: Successive Scale Racing (SSR) optimizes agentic instruction and tool evolution by efficiently selecting evidence combinations, preventing performance degradation in large task pools.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a failure mode in agentic harness evolution where performance degrades as the task pool expands due to suboptimal evidence selection. SSR improves performance as the task pool grows and reduces the number of validation executions required. The method achieved state-of-the-art results across three benchmarks.

items.title: Back Up Before You Regret: Measuring Backup Awareness and Automating Backup in Coding Agents
items.one_liner: BackUpper provides a low-cost, automated backup layer for coding agents to prevent data loss during autonomous task execution.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced RegretBench to measure the 'backup awareness' of coding agents, finding that they rarely preserve state before performing actions that modify it. To address this, they proposed BackUpper, a plug-in layer that automatically checks tool calls and preserves state before modifications occur. BackUpper covers all regret-prone actions with high similarity to original states at a very low cost. The tool can also be configured to respect user preferences regarding which actions to back up.
items.bottom_line: Coding agents lack inherent backup awareness, necessitating external automated backup layers to ensure state reversibility.

items.title: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models
items.one_liner: Standard holistic similarity metrics overstate cross-lingual LLM consistency by up to 67.3%, making trace-level evaluation essential for trustworthy multilingual AI tooling.
items.summary: Researchers introduced a trace-level divergence framework to evaluate multilingual large language models by comparing visible reasoning traces as structured sequences rather than just final answers. They found that standard holistic cosine embeddings systematically overstate agreement, with 52.1% to 67.3% of top-quartile holistic similarity pairs failing to match structural similarity. Human bilingual annotation and same-language controls confirmed that divergence is language-specific and that holistic evaluations overestimate consistency. Consequently, reliable multilingual deployment requires trace-level evaluation to ensure users across different languages receive comparable supporting evidence.
items.bottom_line: Standard holistic evaluations of multilingual LLMs give a false sense of security regarding cross-lingual consistency, necessitating structural trace-level verification.

items.title: SecLog-Bench: A Scalable Benchmark for Cybersecurity Log Reasoning with Scaffolded Evidence
items.one_liner: A new cybersecurity log benchmark reveals that current LLMs struggle with reliable multi-source attack reasoning and step-by-step evidence analysis.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced SecLog-Bench, a scalable benchmark designed to evaluate large language models on cybersecurity log reasoning using multi-source logs and dense step-by-step evidence chains. The platform covers 29 extensible attack scenarios and generates logs from audit, application, and network sources with attack-stage labels. Evaluating eight mainstream LLMs revealed modest performance, with the best model achieving only 44.44% accuracy and 45.07% Macro-F1 for post-detection attack-progress reasoning. Furthermore, models exhibited unreliable reasoning quality, frequently producing correct predictions accompanied by flawed logical chains.
items.bottom_line: Mainstream LLMs achieve low accuracy and unreliable reasoning quality on cybersecurity log analysis tasks even when provided with scaffolded evidence.

items.title: HiMark: Hierarchical and Controllable Multi-bit Watermarking for Large Language Models
items.one_liner: HiMark introduces a hierarchical multi-bit LLM watermarking framework that achieves 90.01% extraction accuracy under paraphrasing attacks.
items.summary: Researchers proposed HiMark, a hierarchical and controllable multi-bit watermarking framework designed to improve provenance tracking and copyright protection for large language models. During watermarking embedding, HiMark uses candidate-control mechanisms including initial sampling, layer-wise tournament elimination, and support-threshold filtering. For detection, a model-agnostic evidence aggregation mechanism accumulates token-level support votes to extract information reliably. Experimental results show that HiMark achieves 90.01% watermark extraction accuracy under paraphrasing attacks when embedding 32 bits within a 300-token text without sacrificing generation quality.
items.bottom_line: Robust multi-bit LLM watermarking is achievable without hurting text quality through hierarchical candidate control and model-agnostic evidence aggregation.

items.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
items.one_liner: A study on continued pre-training for embodied agents across virtual worlds maps the limits of data volume, model size, and cross-world generalization.
items.summary: Researchers studied continued pre-training (CPT) for embodied agents across virtual worlds by analyzing 120 configurations encompassing four model sizes, six data volumes, and five data mixtures. Their findings reveal that larger data volume enhances in-corpus performance, diversity facilitates transfer to related environments, and model size improves data efficiency while affecting generalization to distant worlds. The study identifies an initial cross-world interface phase followed by a narrow world-specific phase, demonstrating that imitation models remain competitive in 3D real-time settings but require advanced training stages beyond CPT to achieve true generalist capabilities.
items.bottom_line: Continued pre-training scaling laws show that while data volume and diversity improve embodied agent transfer, achieving generalist behavior requires new training methods beyond CPT.

items.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
items.one_liner: PAWM provides targeted world model guidance for LLM agents, boosting Claude Sonnet 4.5 task performance significantly.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced the Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM) to steer black-box large language model agents by predicting impending failures and intervening when pitfalls arise. PAWM is trained using supervised fine-tuning on synthetic data followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM in the target environment. The framework improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite. This approach offers targeted guidance for agentic tasks compared to traditional step-by-step observation prediction models.
items.bottom_line: Selectively anticipating pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future vastly improves black-box LLM agent success rates over generic observation prediction.

items.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
items.one_liner: Agent4Sci evaluates frontier coding agents on scientific machine learning benchmarks, showing that they rely on routine ML-engineering tricks rather than domain insight unless equipped with specialized research skills.
items.summary: Frontier coding agents are increasingly used as automated researchers, but improving scientific machine learning models requires complex domain insight rather than routine engineering. Researchers introduced Agent4Sci, a long-horizon testbed across 20 benchmarks and 11 domains to evaluate agents on real-world scientific ML problems. Empirical results show that while frontier models like Claude Opus improve published best models (reaching a 10.4% mean relative improvement), these gains stem almost exclusively from generic ML-engineering tricks rather than true research insights, hindered by novelty miscalibration and resource under-utilization. However, lightweight plug-in skills for research ideation and experiment management significantly boost performance, raising Claude Opus's improvement to 20.1% and Codex to 8.1%.

items.bottom_line: Frontier coding agents can improve scientific machine learning models, but their success currently depends on basic engineering hacks rather than deep scientific reasoning.

items.title: GuideEvolve: Self-Evolving Agent Framework with Expert Guidance and 3Ts Mechanisms
items.one_liner: GuideEvolve introduces the 3Ts mechanisms and expert guidance to optimize self-evolving LLM agent performance and stability.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed GuideEvolve, a self-evolving agent framework that combines expert guidance with three autonomous regulatory mechanisms known as the 3Ts: Think Fast and Slow, Throwback, and Termination by choice. The architecture resolves constraints in current agent models by using a task-specific expert-evaluation pipeline alongside temporal rollback and adaptive optimization protocols. Evaluations on MGSM and MMLU benchmarks show that GuideEvolve achieves high accuracies comparable to the state-of-the-art while cutting required optimization iterations by roughly 50% and lowering variance.
items.bottom_line: GuideEvolve achieves competitive benchmark accuracy while halving required optimization iterations through automated temporal rollbacks and expert evaluation.

claims.text: Empirical validation across the MGSM and MMLU benchmarks demonstrates that GuideEvolve attains performance metrics comparable to current state-of-the-art models.

items.title: Does Every Instance Count Equally? Order Effects in LLM Multi-Instance Processing
items.one_liner: LLM multi-instance processing accuracy can vary by 90 percentage points based on instance order, with models systematically biased toward early inputs.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated fifteen large language models across five datasets and seven instance order patterns to study order bias in multi-instance processing tasks. They discovered substantial order sensitivity, with accuracy differing by roughly 90 percentage points between optimal and suboptimal input arrangements. Models consistently performed better when majority-label instances appeared at the start of the prompt rather than in the middle or end. Reasoning traces and gradient-based attribution scores confirmed that models disproportionately emphasize early and late positions, demonstrating that instance order systematically biases aggregated LLM predictions.
items.bottom_line: Instance order severely skews LLM aggregated predictions, proving that multi-instance evaluations must account for input arrangements.

claims.text: Accuracy can differ by about 90 percentage points between the best and worst order patterns, with models generally more accurate when majority-label instances appear at the start than when they appear in the middle or at the end.

items.title: From Prompts to Posteriors: Can LLM Agents Perform Bayesian Inference in Context?
items.one_liner: LLMs violate Bayes' rule out of the box, but pairing them with reasoning and code execution tools enables principled Bayesian inference for scientific discovery.
items.summary: Large language models are increasingly used across scientific discovery pipelines for tasks like literature synthesis and hypothesis generation, which fundamentally require continuous belief updating via Bayesian inference. While prior assumptions suggested LLMs cannot carry out principled Bayesian belief updating without heuristics, new evaluations show that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule in isolation but improve drastically when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution tools. This capability allows models to closely approximate analytically intractable posteriors. Consequently, LLMs with appropriate tool access can already execute complex belief updates to accelerate AI-powered scientific discovery.
items.bottom_line: Equipping LLMs with code execution and modern reasoning tools unlocks their capacity to perform complex Bayesian belief updates for scientific workflows.

claims.text: Across different scenarios, we find that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule when updating their beliefs in context.
claims.support_span: Across different scenarios, we find that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule when updating their beliefs in context.

claims.text: However, when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution capabilities, their performance drastically improves, enabling even the close approximation of analytically intractable posteriors.
claims.support_span: However, when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution capabilities, their performance drastically improves, enabling even the close approximation of analytically intractable posteriors.

items.title: PreCoMem: Predictive Cognitive Memory for Self-Evolving Long-Term Dialogue Agents
items.one_liner: PreCoMem applies predictive coding principles to long-term LLM dialogue memory, separating transient noise from genuine belief drift via a two-threshold gate.
items.summary: Researchers introduced PreCoMem, a predictive coding-inspired memory consolidation framework for long-term dialogue agents designed to prevent overreaction to transient noise while adapting to genuine user belief drift. PreCoMem computes an Effective Surprisal signal combining semantic deviation and contradiction evidence, scaled down when retrieval is unreliable. A two-threshold gating mechanism categorizes turns into MAINTAIN (reinforcing beliefs), PROFILE (storing ambiguous cues as low-confidence hypotheses in a waiting room), and CORRECT (softly decaying contradicted facts). Evaluations on benchmarks including LoCoMo and a new DiMoBench confirm state-of-the-art accuracy in handling non-stationary belief drift.
key_facts: Evaluated benchmarks: LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S, PersonaMem-v2, DiMoBench
items.bottom_line: Reliable long-term agent memory requires confidence-weighted belief consolidation rather than naive logging or heuristic overwriting.

claims.text: We introduce PreCoMem, a memory consolidation framework inspired by predictive coding that represents memory as confidence-weighted beliefs about the user's state.
claims.support_span: We introduce PreCoMem, a memory consolidation framework inspired by predictive coding that represents memory as confidence-weighted beliefs about the user's state.

claims.text: According to effective surprisal, a two-threshold gate maps each turn to one of three deterministic updates: MAINTAIN reinforces supported beliefs, PROFILE stores ambiguous cues as low-confidence hypotheses, and CORRECT softly decays reliably contradicted facts.
